Київ, атака ввечері 13 жовтня й уночі 14: Kyiv, attack on the evening of 13 October and overnight into 14 October. The first missile wave at about 23:00 hit a nine-storey apartment building in Desnianskyi district, where, according to the State Emergency Service, at least two people had been killed and more than 20 injured at the time of the first report, and 16 residents were evacuated; the fire spread through flats from the first to the eighth floor. According to the Kyiv City Prosecutor’s Office (via Ukrinform, 08:50), three women were killed in Desnianskyi district and one more person in Holosiivskyi district (a non-residential building), i.e. 4 killed and 27 injured; according to Suspilne Kyiv (08:37, citing the military administration, the State Emergency Service and police), 3 killed and 32 injured, 2 killed and 25 injured of them in Desnianskyi district. The discrepancy comes from different timing and counting methods; there are no final figures. Rescue work was continuing in the morning; criminal proceedings have been opened under Art. 438 of the Criminal Code (war crimes). Private houses and apartment buildings, cars, an office building, a café, a library, a stadium and a school were also damaged. No day of mourning was declared (not mentioned in the sources).

Київ, ТЕЦ-4 і житловий будинок, 13–14 жо: Kyiv, CHP-4 and an apartment building, 13–14 October. The first missile wave at about 22:30–23:00 hit CHP-4 (according to Zelensky, one of the city’s main combined heat and power plants) and a nine-storey building in Desnianskyi district; the second series began after 04:00 and lasted several hours (according to the Kyiv Independent, explosions between 04:45 and 06:45). Fires broke out in Dniprovskyi, Darnytskyi and Shevchenkivskyi districts; DTEK introduced emergency outages in five districts, and trams and trolleybuses stopped in part of the city. According to Zelensky, at least 600,000 people in the country are without power, 26 elements of the energy system and four oil and gas facilities were damaged; the strike targeted the energy systems of Kyiv, Kyiv region and Kharkiv. Kyiv and the Air Force say partners did not pass on information about ballistic launches on either 12.10 or 13.10: the missiles were detected by radar only near the city, and the reasons are being investigated. Zelensky called the strike a “demonstrative disrespect” for the United States after the “energy ceasefire” announced by Trump and called for sanctions under Senator Lindsey Graham’s bill and additional Patriot systems. The Air Force clarified that partners had not given warning before each wave (Glavcom, 09:58).

Москва і область, ніч на 14 жовтня. За м: Moscow and the region, night of 14 October. According to Mayor Sergei Sobyanin (via RBC-Ukraine, 08:33), from 20:30 on 13.10 to 07:00 on 14.10, 493 drones flew towards the Moscow region, and another 180 were shot down closer to the capital; there were about ten waves, and TASS called it one of the largest attacks in two years (claimed by russia). Sheremetyevo, Domodedovo, Vnukovo and Zhukovsky temporarily suspended operations, Vnukovo was closed for more than eight hours; Zn.ua reports more than 400 cancelled and delayed flights. The local authorities effectively confirmed a massive attack and airport disruption, but did not name any sites hit or report casualties. As of the morning of 14.10 the General Staff, SBU, HUR, SSO and USF had not confirmed the strike, and the targets are unknown, so this is only an indirect sign of its scale.

Трамп призупинив «пекельні санкції» за з: Trump suspended the “hellish sanctions” under the Graham law two days before they were due to start. By an executive order of 16 October Trump formally imposed, but immediately suspended, 100% tariffs on goods from the largest buyers of russian oil and gas and 500% tariffs on russian energy under the “Lindsey Graham Sanctioning russia and Iran Act of 2026”, which he himself signed on 18 September. The stated basis is a certification to Congress that waiving them “at this stage” is in the US national interest; the tariffs were to take effect after 18 October. The order does not lift previously imposed sanctions, and the suspension has no set end date. Санкції за «законом Грема». Указом від п: Sanctions under the “Graham law”. By an executive order of Friday, 16 October, implementing the “Lindsey Graham Sanctioning russia and Iran Act of 2026” (Trump signed it on 18 September), the US president formally imposed and then immediately suspended 100% tariffs on goods from the largest buyers of russian oil and gas, 500% tariffs on russian energy and sanctions on a number of russian entities. The legal basis is section 115 of the act, which allows the president to waive the measures subject to a written certification to Congress that this is in the US national interest. The suspension remains in force until Trump or the Secretary of State decides otherwise; the order does not touch previously imposed sanctions. Ukrinform (06:33 17.10) and Newsweek link the decision to Trump’s diesel deal with Putin of 9 October; the order itself does not mention diesel, and the White House has not confirmed a causal link. According to Ukrinform, 12 senators from both parties this week urged Trump to cancel the deal with Putin and enforce the law; Republican congressman Michael McCaul called the intention to lower diesel prices understandable but warned that easing pressure on russian oil would “only fund the Kremlin’s war machine”. Experts cited by Novaya Gazeta Europe consider the law largely symbolic, but the first significant increase in pressure on the kremlin during Trump’s term.

Sanctions under the “Graham law”: a new detail. Secretary of State Marco Rubio on 18 October (according to the Kyiv Independent) described the suspension of tariffs and sanctions, which Trump formalised by executive order on 16.10, as a 60-day period to analyse the effects of imposing sanctions and tariffs simultaneously, citing high global energy prices due to the US war with Iran. Earlier, according to the text of the order (Ukrinform, Newsweek), the suspension had no set term, lasting until the president or the secretary of state decide otherwise — see “discrepancies”. Reaction: according to headlines in Axios (17.10), the Washington Post and CNN, the decision drew instant bipartisan criticism in Congress; Zelensky, according to a CNBC headline, called it “wrong”. kremlin special envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it a “historic moment” (see “What they say in the swamps”).

Starlink. За Axios, 17 жовтня Зеленський: Starlink. According to Axios, on 17 October Zelensky said that Starlink use in Ukraine remains partly restricted: military tests on Friday showed that a connected vehicle kept its link at 180 km/h in EU countries, while in Ukraine the signal dropped at 161 km/h; he called it a “planned operation”. The restrictions prevent using drones to intercept russian drones and supplying troops. According to Reuters (15.10, anonymous US and Western officials), the order to slow Starshield came from inside the White House; the White House and Trump (16.10) deny involvement, and The Telegraph writes that Musk proposed the restrictions to Trump — the White House called this “totally false”. Ukraine’s chief negotiator Rustem Umerov discussed it with Jared Kushner on Friday; according to Axios, they also talked about a meeting of the US and Ukrainian teams planned for next week on Trump’s proposal to end the war.
Заморожені російські активи. Відповідаюч: Frozen russian assets. Answering journalists’ questions on 17 October (according to Obozrevatel), Zelensky said Kyiv has information about russia’s attempts, through certain partners, to recover or unfreeze part of the frozen assets, but all details have been discussed with the Europeans, and the issue is now “under Europe’s full control”.
Втрати у війні. Відповідаючи на запитанн: War losses. Answering journalists’ questions on Friday 16 October (according to Ukrinform, 17.10; location not given), Trump repeated that he knows the “details” of the war and will one day make them public, that he is interested only in ending the war, and said that on average about 25,000 soldiers a month die in it, and last month 32,000. He did not say where the figures come from or whether they cover both sides’ losses. For comparison, Ukraine’s General Staff claims 46,230 russian losses (killed and wounded combined) for September — not independently verified.
